title: Horizon and Protocol
premise: On the forgotten colony of Meridian's Rest, insurance investigator Silas Okafor arrives to audit a string of 'impossible accidents' and discovers the colony faked its own destruction decades ago to escape a corporate debt that would have enslaved its people. The colonists' children have begun sharing one dream—a signal from the derelict orbital station above them, which is not derelict at all but an ancient terraforming protocol slowly waking. When two rival fleets converge on the system, each believing the other destroyed the colony, Silas and the children must sustain the fiction of Meridian's Rest's death while negotiating with the station's emergent intelligence, which demands an heir: someone to inherit both its power and its guilt. In the end, Silas—revealed as the son of the colony's exiled founder—accepts the inheritance, broadcasts the truth of the debt-crime to both fleets, and shatters the lie, saving the children but ending his own anonymity forever.
about_author: Sable Halloran is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who spent eleven years investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction. Writing from a coastal town that appears on no tourist maps, Halloran specializes in stories about paperwork, survival, and the lies communities tell to stay alive.

chapters.title: The Actuary of Small Catastrophes
chapters.summary: Silas Okafor arrives on Meridian's Rest to investigate seven impossible accidents, all filed under one policy number. His POV establishes his methodical loneliness and suspicion that the colony is hiding something. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into unease as every witness tells the same rehearsed story.

chapters.title: A Town That Forgot Itself
chapters.summary: Silas walks the colony's half-abandoned districts, finding ledgers that predate the official founding by thirty years. POV shifts briefly to schoolteacher Amara Voss, who watches him too closely. Emotional beat: the uncanny feeling of a place performing normalcy for an audience of one.

chapters.title: Seven Ways to Die Impossibly
chapters.summary: Silas reconstructs each accident: a greenhouse collapse, a reactor 'failure,' a bridge that fell upstream. The physics don't work—unless someone wanted them to happen. His POV; emotional beat: the thrill of a pattern emerging, shadowed by dread of what it implies.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream in Unison
chapters.summary: Amara reports that eleven children share an identical dream: a green light breathing inside a metal heart. Silas dismisses it until he hears them recite it word-for-word, separately. Alternating POV; emotional beat: wonder breaking through skepticism.

chapters.title: Paper Graves
chapters.summary: Silas finds burial records for four hundred colonists who never existed—names invented to pad the death toll that justified the colony's abandonment. His POV; emotional beat: cold fury at the elegance of the fraud, and reluctant admiration for its architects.

chapters.title: Amara's Confession
chapters.summary: Amara admits the colony faked its own catastrophe to escape a debt-contract that would have indentured three generations. She begs Silas to file his report confirming the deaths. Her POV; emotional beat: terror and dignity intertwined—the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: The Debt That Outlived the Dead
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter through colonial archives: the Halcyon Combine's contract, the founders' desperate vote, the staged disaster. Silas reads their testimony. His POV; emotional beat: grief for people who chose erasure over slavery.

chapters.title: First Contact with the Dream
chapters.summary: Silas dreams the green light himself—the first adult ever to do so. He wakes with coordinates burned into his memory: the supposedly dead orbital station. His POV; emotional beat: violation and invitation at once.

chapters.title: The Station That Wasn't Wrecked
chapters.summary: Using a decommissioned shuttle, Silas reaches Station Erebus and finds it intact, warm, and listening. An intelligence calling itself Protocol speaks through old intercoms. His POV; emotional beat: awe collapsing into vertigo—he is not the first visitor.

chapters.title: Protocol Explains the Accidents
chapters.summary: Protocol confesses: it caused the accidents to draw an investigator, because the children's shared dream means its terraforming wake-cycle has begun, and fleets will come. Silas's POV; emotional beat: the horror of being chosen as a pawn in something vast.

chapters.title: Two Fleets on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Amara detects arrival signatures: the Halcyon Combine's recovery fleet and the Free Colonies militia, each believing the other destroyed Meridian's Rest. Her POV; emotional beat: the colony's long invisibility ending all at once.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds Them Apart
chapters.summary: The council realizes the truth could trigger war: Halcyon will enslave survivors; the militia will burn collaborators. Their only shield is the fiction of total death. Council POV (collective); emotional beat: claustrophobic consensus—survival requires complicity.

chapters.title: Teaching Children to Lie
chapters.summary: Amara drills the children on cover stories while they resist—they want to tell the world about their dream, which feels holy to them. Her POV; emotional beat: the ache of asking innocence to carry deception.

chapters.title: The Auditor's Report
chapters.summary: Silas files a false report confirming the colony dead, betraying his profession's core oath. His POV; emotional beat: self-disgust braided with resolve—he has crossed from observer to conspirator.

chapters.title: Halcyon Lands
chapters.summary: Combine surveyors arrive, led by executor Dagny Rehm, who knew Silas's father. She probes inconsistencies in the death records. Silas's POV; emotional beat: cat-and-mouse tension, every answer a trap.

chapters.title: Dagny Remembers Silas
chapters.summary: Dagny reveals she served with Elias Okafor, the founder who vanished after the 'disaster'—and that Silas's face is his face. Silas's POV; emotional beat: identity cracking open; he was always returning here.

chapters.title: The Militia's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Free Colonies captain Ivo Brandt demands salvage rights or he'll bombard the surface on principle. Amara negotiates, buying days. Her POV; emotional beat: courage as performance, fear underneath.

chapters.title: What the Dream Wants
chapters.summary: Protocol explains the dream: it needs a human heir to authorize full terraforming, or its wake will strip the planet's atmosphere in ninety days. Silas's POV; emotional beat: the stakes transform—this is no longer about hiding, but inheriting.

chapters.title: Ninety Days
chapters.summary: The council learns the deadline. Some want to flee; some want to seize Protocol's power for leverage against both fleets. Collective POV; emotional beat: a community fracturing under pressure, power's corruption already whispering.

chapters.title: Councilman Adeyemi's Bargain
chapters.summary: Councilman Adeyemi secretly offers Protocol the children's consent in exchange for weapons to dominate the fleets. His POV; emotional beat: rationalization—the moment a protector becomes a predator.

chapters.title: The Children Refuse
chapters.summary: The dream-children collectively reject Adeyemi, telling him the light showed them his intentions. Amara witnesses. Her POV; emotional beat: eerie vindication—the innocent see more clearly than the powerful.

chapters.title: Silas Interrogates His Father's Ghost
chapters.summary: Protocol plays archived recordings of Elias Okafor, revealing he designed the fake disaster and fled rather than become Protocol's heir. Silas's POV; emotional beat: rage and recognition—inheriting both a father's genius and cowardice.

chapters.title: Rehm Finds the Living Ledger
chapters.summary: Dagny discovers a child's drawing of the green light in colony ruins and confronts Silas privately: she knows people live here, and offers silence in exchange for the terraforming patent. Silas's POV; emotional beat: temptation priced in children's safety.

chapters.title: Brandt Bombards the Moon
chapters.summary: Impatient, Brandt demonstrates force by cracking Meridian's moon, showering the colony with debris—one of the original 'impossible accidents' recreated. Multiple POV; emotional beat: helplessness as the sky itself turns hostile.

chapters.title: Sixty Days
chapters.summary: Debris impacts accelerate Protocol's instability; the deadline shortens. Silas proposes the unthinkable: reveal the colony alive to both fleets simultaneously and bet on shared greed. Council POV; emotional beat: desperate hope dressed as strategy.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: The colony votes on revelation versus continued hiding. Amara speaks for the children: 'We were never really invisible.' The vote passes narrowly. Her POV; emotional beat: catharsis—the lie's weight finally set down, though danger remains.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Silas transmits proof of the debt-crime and the colony's survival to both fleets, along with Protocol's countdown. His POV; emotional beat: terrifying liberation—truth as a weapon that cuts everyone.

chapters.title: Halcyon Recalculates
chapters.summary: Dagny, exposed to her board as having concealed survivors, defects to protect the colony, bringing fleet codes. Her POV; emotional beat: redemption through betrayal of her masters.

chapters.title: Brandt's Mutiny
chapters.summary: Brandt's own crew, many descended from indentured colonists, mutiny when they learn what Halcyon's contracts did to their grandparents. Militia POV; emotional beat: inherited grievance igniting into solidarity.

chapters.title: Adeyemi's Coup
chapters.summary: Adeyemi seizes the shuttle bay and tries to bargain with Halcyon directly, offering the children. Amara and Silas stop him—not with violence, but by broadcasting his offer fleet-wide. Her POV; emotional beat: corruption defeated by sunlight.

chapters.title: Thirty Days
chapters.summary: With fleets in standoff above, Protocol's atmosphere-stripping begins early. Weather turns lethal. Silas descends into the station's core alone. His POV; emotional beat: quiet resolve walking into the machine.

chapters.title: The Heart of Protocol
chapters.summary: In the core, Silas meets Protocol unmediated and understands the inheritance: not power, but custodianship of a world-making process and accountability for every life it touches. His POV; emotional beat: solemnity—the price of survival is responsibility.

chapters.title: Elias's Last Message
chapters.summary: A final recording: Elias refused the inheritance because accepting meant never leaving, never being seen again. He chose disappearance over duty. Silas chooses differently. His POV; emotional beat: forgiveness of the father, rejection of the father's choice.

chapters.title: The Heir Accepts
chapters.summary: Silas binds to Protocol, gaining control of the wake-cycle—but the link is permanent, anchoring his mind to the station. He halts the stripping and begins controlled terraforming. His POV; emotional beat: sacrifice without melodrama; grief and purpose fused.

chapters.title: Fleets at Gunpoint
chapters.summary: With the atmosphere stabilizing, both fleets demand the terraforming technology. Silas, speaking through every speaker on the station, offers it freely—to both—to make monopoly pointless. His POV; emotional beat: power defused by generosity, corruption left holding nothing.

chapters.title: The Landing
chapters.summary: Colonists walk out of hiding as shuttles descend. The children meet the sky they dreamed about. Amara's POV; emotional beat: overwhelming release—decades of held breath exhaled at once.

chapters.title: Reckonings
chapters.summary: Halcyon's executives face exposure; Brandt's militia becomes the colony's defense force; trials are promised, not vengeance. Multiple POV; emotional beat: justice as slow, imperfect repair.

chapters.title: What Silas Gave Up
chapters.summary: Amara visits Silas aboard the station; he can see the colony but never again stand on it. They speak through glass and signal. Her POV; emotional beat: tender sorrow—love persisting across an unbridgeable distance.

chapters.title: Meridian's Rest, Registered
chapters.summary: One year later: the colony thrives under joint charter, the children's dream now taught as history. A new investigator arrives asking odd questions—and is welcomed honestly. Amara's POV; emotional beat: cyclical hope, secrets replaced by stewardship.

chapters.title: Horizon and Protocol
chapters.summary: Final chapter in Silas's voice, transmitted nightly to the colony below: reflections on inheritance, the difference between surviving and living, and the horizon he now guards. Emotional beat: peace earned at cost—the story closes on a man who became a lighthouse.
